Date: 2026-04-11
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (CTO - Acme), Maya Singh (ML Eng), Alan Park (Infra)
Recording: Fireflies.ai auto-transcript
Notes: Casual discovery focused on Redwood quickstart, free credits, time-to-first-token and feasibility of Dedicated/Private later.
summary: Acme is evaluating Redwood for initial PLG/self-serve adoption (quickstart) with intent to scale to Dedicated or Private in 6-12 months depending on cost and security. Key asks: how long to get first token using Redwood hosted API, how free credits work, latency/cost tradeoffs, and what network/SOC2 docs we can share. SE asked for sample workload and will run a latency/cost estimate; AE to send quickstart resources and SOC2/network docs.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Latency vs cost, batching and quantization
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia from Redwood, AE on the account, with Liam our SE. Quick check, audio good?
[00:08] Jordan: Yep, all good. Thanks.
[00:11] Sofia: Awesome. So goal for today is to run through the quickstart experience, answer questions about free credits, and understand what you need to get to a POC. No heavy slides, we'll keep it convo.
[00:25] Liam: Hi all, I'll mostly cover technical bits, latency, cost tradeoffs, and what Dedicated/Private would look like down the road.
[00:33] Maya: Great, we want to validate how fast we can ship something with Redwood hosted API first.
[00:38] Sofia: Perfect, that's common. Typical workflow: sign up, create API key, claim free credits, call the text-gen/chat endpoint, get first token in minutes if you follow quickstart. We have SDKs too.
[00:52] Jordan: Quick question on free credits — how much and any throttles?
[00:57] Sofia: We typically give X credits for quick evaluation — that'll cover a few thousand tokens of testing. There's a default rate limit on new accounts but it's usually high enough to validate. If you need higher burst we can temporarily lift it for the POC.
[01:12] Alan: Can you spell out the path to get from hosted to Dedicated or Private? We have compliance reqs and may need VPC later.
[01:20] Liam: Sure, short answer: start with Hosted to get quick time-to-first-token and iterate. If you need predictable throughput and tenant isolation, Dedicated is next — reserved GPU pools. Private is available for VPC or on-prem with a customer-managed control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs.
[01:40] Maya: Any gotchas for model compatibility? We run shorter prompts but high token rates.
[01:45] Liam: We'll ask for your prompt distribution — that matters for batching and KV cache. We recommend quantization profiles for cost, and our runtime picks kernels based on sequence length. With short prompts you get higher qps per GPU.
[01:57] Jordan: What's typical latency for the hosted API? We want sub-200ms for single-turn generation if possible.
[02:03] Liam: Depends on model and sequence length. For our curated small-to-medium open models, 100–250ms is realistic for 1–2 token outputs; larger models or longer outputs increase latency. We can run a benchmark with your prompt set and target sequence lengths.
[02:18] Sofia: Also note, streaming vs non-streaming affects observed latencies. If you need tail latency SLAs, Dedicated with reserved capacity is easier to guarantee.
[02:29] Maya: About security, what docs can you share? We need SOC 2, network architecture, SSO.
[02:34] Sofia: We'll send SOC 2 report, SSO/SAML setup guide, and a network diagram that shows how Redwood Hosted handles VPC egress and TLS. For Private, we have details on KMS/HSM integrations and audit log retention.
[02:50] Alan: We use strict egress rules. For hosted, can you support private networking or IP allowlist?
[02:56] Liam: Hosted supports IP allowlist and customer-specific VPC peering for higher tiers; Dedicated gives more control. Private is for full VPC/on-prem. We'll capture the exact firewall rules you need.
[03:10] Jordan: What's the cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated? Rough numbers to justify moving.
[03:16] Sofia: Hosted is usage-based — per-token and embeddings. Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract (monthly/annual) which lowers per-token unit cost for sustained throughput. We can share a sample calc. Liam will run a model based on your 5k qps hypothetical.
[03:30] Liam: Right — throw us your expected qps and average token per request and we'll produce a cost/latency table with recommended batch sizes and quantization.
[03:40] Maya: How quick is the quickstart in practice? Minutes, hours?
[03:44] Sofia: From account creation to first token is typically under 30 minutes if you follow the quickstart with SDK. For teams with SSO org provisioning it can be faster once SSO is set up.
[03:55] Jordan: Any common transcription errors I should be aware of? (laughter)
[03:58] Sofia: (laughs) Fireflies sometimes messes up product names — sometimes it writes 'Redwood infer' or 'Redwood runtime' but you get the idea.
[04:06] Liam: Back to technical — about caching: we do prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts which can drastically reduce cost for few-shot templates. Also continuous batching in the runtime to improve throughput.
[04:20] Maya: Do you support function/tool calling or structured output? We want to return JSON from the model.
[04:26] Liam: Yes we support structured output and tool calling primitives on the hosted API. For more complex tool chains, Dedicated gives better isolation for webhook endpoints.
[04:36] Jordan: If we start with hosted and then need to move to Dedicated mid-POC, is the API surface consistent?
[04:41] Sofia: Yes — same API surface and SDKs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, which is why teams like Redwood: the switch is mostly infra/contract, not app changes.
[04:52] Alan: Any limitations around data retention or log access for hosted? We need to know what stays in logs.
[04:59] Sofia: Hosted has configurable retention and can redact logs at token-level for privacy. For strict retention and complete control, Private is the path. We'll include log retention options in the docs.
[05:12] Maya: For the quickstart, do you provide example prompt sets or eval harness?
[05:17] Liam: Yes — we have quickstart templates, sample prompts, and an eval harness so you can run basic quality checks and regression tests. We'll share the repo link.
[05:26] Jordan: What's the on-ramp for engineering? How much support do you provide during trial?
[05:31] Sofia: Self-serve first, with docs and SDKs. AE/SE will assist for POC scoping and can open limited onboarding sessions. For Dedicated/Private there's more hands-on support in the contract.
[05:42] Maya: Are there any rate limits that block us from realistic load tests?
[05:46] Liam: New accounts have soft limits but we raise them for POCs. For very large load tests we recommend a staging Dedicated or an arranged hosted increase.
[05:56] Jordan: We're also comparing to OpenAI — what would you say are the differences?
[06:01] Sofia: Main differences are: Redwood is inference-platform focused with a single runtime across modes, more transparent performance benchmarks and tooling for cost optimization like batching and quantization. OpenAI is model-first and has different pricing/SLAs. We also support easier Dedicated/Private deployments.
[06:18] Alan: Any concerns about latency if we go with hosted in us-west?
[06:22] Liam: For us-west region it's comparable; if you need the lowest tail latencies you can pin to specific regions or use Dedicated. We'll include region performance numbers.
[06:31] Maya: Ok sounds good. What do you need from us to run the latency/cost estimate?
[06:35] Liam: A sample of prompts, expected tokens per request, expected qps distribution over day, and SLA targets. Jordan indicated they'll share that.
[06:44] Jordan: I'll put together a small sample set and traffic profile.
[06:47] Sofia: Great. We'll follow up with links: quickstart guide, free credits claim, SOC 2, network diagram, and a proposed time for the Dedicated sizing call.
[06:58] Maya: One more question — do you support SSO/scim for user provisioning into the console?
[07:03] Sofia: Yes we support SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning for user accounts, RBAC in console. We'll attach the SSO setup doc.
[07:12] Alan: For Private, what does deployment look like? Is it a container image or managed appliance?
[07:18] Liam: Private can be delivered as a customer-managed control plane using our on-prem package and deployable containers; we integrate with KMS and provide audit log shipping. We'll share the architecture doc.
[07:30] Jordan: Ok let's recap next steps.
[07:33] Sofia: Recap: Sofia sends quickstart + free credits + SOC2/network docs; Liam runs latency/cost calc based on traffic profile; Jordan shares sample prompts and schedule for sizing call.
[07:45] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:48] Sofia: Thanks all, we'll follow up by end of tomorrow with materials.
[07:52] Jordan: Thanks, bye.
[07:53] End of recording.

Notes on transcript: occasional mislabels and minor transcription errors (product names, acronyms). Some timestamps approximate; content remains faithful to conversation about quickstart and POC scoping.
